rv.q: This is a production that ‘does the play’: clearly, succinctly and without much in the way of authorial intervention or interpretive angle.
It’s a tragedy shaped as much by complicity as intent, and this staging’s greatest strength lies in how recognisably human the roots of evil feel.

The production rattles through at just over two hours and, while never quite reaching the heights of last year’s The Winter’s Tale , is an accessible and engaging account of one of the bard’s most perfect texts.

cn.t: Mixed reviews for this ensemble-driven Macbeth: critics praise its fresh focus on enablers over the lead, but find McLoughlin miscast—his warmth clashing with the role's darkness.
